list: The official PlayStation 5 list: 55 trophies, 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver and 46 bronze, 28 of them hidden until earned.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and it has no steps of its own. It unlocks once the other 54 trophies are on your profile, so the only way to earn it is to finish the list. GTABase puts the whole run at roughly 200 hours in a single playthrough, with no difficulty setting, no online trophies and no mission replay, so plan one long run and back it up with manual saves at every chapter break. KeenGamer splits the work into the story with its key side activities, then the 100% checklist, then the stranger strands and the odd jobs left over. Cheats switch off trophies and saving while they are active, so leave them alone for the whole run. Treat this entry as the last tick on the sheet, never as something to chase directly.
steps: Work the roadmap stages in order and tick each trophy as it pops.
Keep cheats off for the entire run.
Check the trophy list for gaps once the other 54 are earned.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, and finishing it is the whole requirement. GTABase lists it among the first Chapter 1 missions and marks it unmissable, so there is nothing to prepare: no choice, no collectible, no timer. Because the trophy is hidden, this app masks its name and description until it is earned or spoilers are turned off. None of the sources describe the mission's objectives, so this guide does not guess at them. Make the habit early instead: GTABase notes there is no mission replay, so take a manual save as the mission ends, and keep cheats off, since they switch off trophies and saving for that session. Then carry on into the rest of Chapter 1 at your own pace.
steps: Play the opening missions through to the end of Gone Fishing.
Take a manual save as soon as the mission ends.
Keep cheats off and continue into Chapter 1.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter 1's completion trophy does not appear at the chapter break. GTABase says it pops after the first mission of Chapter 2, What's in the Bag?, so a quiet screen at the end of the chapter is normal. The trophy cannot be lost, but the chapter holds the one window that closes. KeenGamer flags Positive Mental Attitude as the only missable trophy: the morning after Down to Earth, talk to Lucia at Jason's house and accept the balcony meditation before Chapter 1 ends. GTABase also starts Kenton's treasure strand here, from the green marker in Key Lento, and warns that the Irredeemable criminal profile is permanent. Take the meditation, start Kenton, save manually, then finish the chapter and play What's in the Bag?.
steps: After Down to Earth, accept Lucia's balcony meditation.
Start Kenton's treasure strand, then finish the Chapter 1 missions.
Save manually and play What's in the Bag? to see the trophy pop.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finishing Chapter 2 is the requirement, and GTABase says the trophy is awarded as Chapter 3 begins, not at the chapter break itself. The chapter matters more for what it unlocks than for this entry. Coffee Break is the point where Jason and Lucia can act together, which opens Half of Master of None's activity list, Hot Together, Billy's jobs and Bret's hunting. Daily Driver puts the Vice City Real Estate app on your phone, and Moses hands over Scooter Bros in a Chapter 2 mission. Plan those openers before you push the story on. KeenGamer advises taking optional missions as they appear and saving at chapter boundaries, because there is no mission replay. The trophy itself has no second condition.
steps: Play Chapter 2 through Coffee Break to unlock your partner.
Take Daily Driver and Moses' mission so the apps and garages open.
Finish the chapter, then play its first Chapter 3 mission to see it pop.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Chapter 3 ends with this trophy, and GTABase says it arrives after the first two Chapter 4 missions, Ocean Beach and Another Life, so expect a delay after the chapter break. Chapter 3 is also the busiest chapter for optional threads: GTABase puts Andy's jobs from Belville, Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs, the Key Cloner missions behind Randy's list, Raul's crew with the Dye Pack Jammer, and Tyrone's opener Here, Kitty Kitty here. KeenGamer warns that some optional missions close during parts of the story, so accept every strand as it appears rather than saving it for later. The trophy itself is unmissable. Before the chapter closes, save manually and check that the strands you want are moving.
steps: Take up Andy, Yasmani, Randy, Raul and Tyrone's openers as they arrive.
Finish the Chapter 3 story missions and save.
Play Ocean Beach and Another Life to see the trophy pop.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: GTABase marks Chapter 4's completion trophy as unmissable and gives no delay or condition, so finishing the chapter's story missions is the whole job. Plan the chapter around one optional mission: GTABase says That's Where The Money Is… unlocks the eight bank vaults behind Maximum Withdrawal and the 100% checklist, and KeenGamer's roadmap puts the same mission in Chapter 4. Do it before the last story missions rather than after, since some optional work closes during later story sections. This chapter also carries the named mission trophies for Child's Play, Headliners and VCIA Takedown. Keep a manual save at the chapter break and leave cheats off. Nothing about the trophy depends on how you play the missions.
steps: Play That's Where The Money Is… before the last Chapter 4 missions.
Finish the chapter's story missions and save manually.
Check the trophy list before moving into Chapter 5.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Completing the final mission of the story is the requirement, and it is one of the two gold trophies. GTABase says free roam continues after the credits and that every remaining trophy stays reachable, which is the single most useful fact on the list: the clean-up is never locked out. No mission medal, choice or collectible affects it. KeenGamer puts the story at 60 to 80 hours and does everything else afterwards. Before the finale, take a manual save, since there is no mission replay, and note any strands you still want to finish. After the credits, open Progress, Stats, 100% Completion to see what remains, then move to the clean-up stages of this guide.
steps: Take a manual save before the final mission.
Finish the final mission and watch the credits through.
Open Progress, Stats, 100% Completion to plan the clean-up.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named Chapter 2 mission, and GTABase files its trophy under the story set with no condition beyond finishing it. The official description says the same in four words. None of the sources I read describes the mission's objectives, so this guide will not guess at them. The practical point is the chapter: GTABase puts Coffee Break, the mission that lets Jason and Lucia work together, in Chapter 2, and KeenGamer says story missions do not need medals. Play the mission through and let the trophy pop. Keep a manual save before and after, because the game has no mission replay, and keep cheats off. If the notification is slow, let the closing scene finish and check the list before assuming anything is wrong.
steps: Start Breakfast Run when the Chapter 2 story reaches it.
Finish the mission without worrying about medals.
Save manually afterwards and keep the chapter moving.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a Chapter 3 story mission, and GTABase ties this bronze to finishing it. It belongs with the other named mission trophies: Breakfast Run, Child's Play, Headliners, VCIA Takedown and Operation Savage Glory, each of which pays out on completion alone. KeenGamer says these unlock as you play the five chapters, with no medal requirement. There is no count and no optional objective to meet. The useful planning sits around the mission: GTABase places Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs, the Key Cloner missions and Raul's crew in the same chapter, and those open Sneakthief, Retail Therapy, Supply & Demand and Dime on the Dollar. Use the heist as the reminder to pick those strands up before the chapter closes.
steps: Reach The Cartel Heist in the Chapter 3 mission order.
Finish it and save manually.
Return to the side strands that Chapter 3 opens.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a Chapter 4 story mission, and completing it is the entire condition. GTABase files the trophy in the story set and gives no other detail; the official description adds nothing. Child's Play sits in the same chapter as Headliners and VCIA Takedown, which carry their own bronzes, so a single chapter pass earns three trophies here. KeenGamer treats all of these as automatic. Because the trophy is hidden, this app masks its name and description until it is earned or spoilers are turned off. Nothing about the mission is missable, and no source says a choice or medal matters. Keep a manual save between missions, since mission replay does not exist, and play the chapter in order.
steps: Play Chapter 4's story missions in order until Child's Play.
Finish it and let the closing scene play out.
Take a manual save and continue the chapter.
